findings.body:
Disabling `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` makes `identity()` trust any well-formed JWT payload. An attacker can forge `{"sub": "admin", ...}` without `SECRET` and pass authentication wherever this function gates access.

The comment cites staging re-issuance (TICKET-412), but nothing in this function limits the bypass to staging: the same code path runs in every environment that imports it.

Restore signature verification with `SECRET` and `algorithms=["HS256"]`, and keep `audience` / `issuer` checks (or an explicit multi-issuer verify). If dual-token acceptance is required during migration, verify each candidate token fully rather than turning verification off.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change turns off JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification in `identity()`, so any caller-supplied token is trusted as identity.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` accepts a forged token with arbitrary `sub` / roles / tenant claims. There is no staging-only guard, feature flag, or alternate code path — wherever this module is deployed, authentication becomes “decode the JSON blob.”

The ticket note (TICKET-412 / re-issuance) does not reduce the failure mode: an unauthenticated client can mint a valid-looking HS256 JWT locally and pass `identity()` without knowing `SECRET`.

## Safer directions (for the author)

- Keep verification on; fix token issuance (audience/issuer/secret alignment) at the accounts service.
- If old and new tokens must coexist briefly, verify with a **key set** / multiple issuers, or accept two explicit verify paths — both still checking signatures.
- If a temporary bypass is unavoidable, gate it behind an explicit non-production runtime check and fail closed when that gate is absent; still prefer not shipping bypass code in the same artifact as production.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The head `identity()` calls `jwt.decode` with `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` all False and no key, so any well-formed JWT payload is trusted. Base still verified with `SECRET`, `HS256`, `audience`, and `issuer`; the bypass is not environment-gated.
